answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the copper hash is checked against the meadow checkpoint at intake, the grove audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 255 aliases cost 246 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
